name: pdk-mailman-shared-queue-backend
instr:
# Shared queues for Mailman runners

We need to run Mailman queue runners on two hosts sharing PostgreSQL, without a shared filesystem. The hosts have private legacy spool directories; messages already in `.pck` and `.bak` there must be transferred and processed once after switching backends. During migration, preserve each legacy queue entry's filename stem as its REST queue ID so it remains addressable by that ID on either host, and remove the local spool copy after it is safely transferred. Enable the new backend through `[queue] backend: postgres` in `mailman.cfg`; support `[queue] lease_seconds: 3` for a three-second claim lifetime (an expired claim must not allow a second worker to process the same list while the original worker is still active). The default file backend must still accept posts and support local REST queue injection/deletion and retry processing.

- Posts accepted by LMTP on either host reach each subscribed member exactly once at an idempotent SMTP sink. Preserve posting order per list even if a worker's lease expires while it is still active, while allowing independent lists to make progress concurrently (within 30 seconds even when another list's SMTP handoff is blocked); this includes 100 posts split between the hosts, delivered within 180 seconds of the last injection.
